$comment: ACCEPTED STRENGTH STATE, per lift, in Pelland Table 4 fractional sets.
Same contract as coverage-baseline.json: a gate expected to fail cannot signal a regression, so this
records what was accepted and gym-strength.mjs fails only on movement away from it.
RE-ACCEPTED 2026-09-01 for the programme rebuilt against the direct-set floor. The sum past the point
of detectable increments went 79.5 to 113.0. That is the largest single move this file has recorded,
so it is written up rather than waved through: the one thing this gate cannot check is an --accept
that should not have happened.
WHERE THE 33.5 SETS CAME FROM, and 25 of them are not a move at all:
Back Extension     +13.5   A NEW LIFT ON THE LIST, not a lift that moved.
Leg Curl Machine    +3.5   Also new. The only knee flexion in the week; every other hamstring
exposure is a hinge, so half of what that muscle does was untrained.
the six that moved   +8    Documented shared-glutes mechanism: any lower-body set raises the
fractional count of every lift that shares the glutes, which here is
nearly all of them. Their DIRECT sets did not rise. The back squat is
on 6 direct sets in both the old week and this one.
WHY IT WAS ACCEPTED. All eight sit 3 to 20 fractional sets past the point where Pelland stops finding
detectable increments, and section 4.3 calls past that point a price rather than a wall. A move from
20.5 to 23.5 is on a part of the curve where the paper measured nothing. What it buys is measured and
is not on a flat part of anything: FOUR MUSCLES THAT FAILED THE SOURCED FLOOR NOW CLEAR IT. Adductors
3 to 6, rhomboids and mid traps 3 to 6, front delts 3 to 6, triceps 3 to 6, with hamstrings 9 to 12
and lats 6 to 9 on top.
THE FIFTH MUSCLE, THE SPINAL ERECTORS, IS STILL AT ZERO AND THAT IS NOT A PROGRAMME FAILURE. The
first version of this rebuild put two blocks of back extension in the week on the strength of a
catalogue override calling the erectors a prime mover of it. The override carried a jointActionNote
saying nobody had confirmed it, and it did not survive: with a flat spine the joint action is HIP
extension and the erectors work isometrically, the same role they have in the squat, the row and the
RDL, where this catalogue calls them secondary. The attribution was corrected instead of leaned on.
See the erectors entry in targets.json.
A SCOPING QUESTION ABOUT THIS GATE, RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE. `l.loadable` is read
from movements.json, so any lower-body-primary lift the catalogue calls loadable lands on a STRENGTH
table denominated per assessed exercise, whatever the programme actually prescribes. Nobody assesses
lower-body strength with a back extension or a leg curl. The same reasoning already narrowed
PRIORITY_PATTERN once, on 2026-08-31, to keep calf raises and adductor work out. Changing a gate's
scope in the same commit that benefits from the change is the move this project has been burned by,
so it is left alone and written down. If it is fixed later, the fix belongs on the PRESCRIPTION
rather than on an exercise's name.
THE REAL COST IS THE CLOCK, and it should be quoted in those units rather than in fractional sets:
98 prescribed sets to 110, and 53 sets that own the clock to 59, about 11% either way. At his measured
4.0 minutes per logged set that is a median session moving from about 70 minutes to about 78. That is
an extrapolation from the programme this replaces, not a measurement of this one.
WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS THE WRONG CALL: if he reports the sessions running long. There is almost nothing
to cut. Eleven of the fifteen gradeable muscles sit at exactly two slots, so removing any block drops
one of them below the floor of 4. The two cuts that cost nothing on the muscle axis are the box jump,
from five sets to three, which he has already ruled is not volume, and the leg curl, which is surplus
hamstring work above the floor. After those the lever is rest lengths, not blocks.
